subject: Social & Citizenship Studies
content: A family is a group of people who love and care for each other. There are different types of families. A nuclear family has parents and their children living together. An extended family includes grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins living nearby or together. A single-parent family has one parent raising the children. Some children live with grandparents or other relatives. All families are special, no matter how many people are in them. Families help each other, share meals, celebrate festivals, and take care of one another.
summary: Family types: nuclear (parents and children), extended (includes grandparents, aunts, uncles), single-parent (one parent). All families are special and loving.
learning_objectives: Understand that all families are valuable
Appreciate how families care for each other
nigerian_examples: Nigerian extended families often living in the same compound
Children spending holidays with grandparents in the village
Aunts and uncles helping raise nieces and nephews

quiz_questions.question: What is a nuclear family?
quiz_questions.explanation: A nuclear family has parents and their children living in one home.

quiz_questions.question: What is an extended family?
options: Parents, children, grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins
quiz_questions.correct_answer: Parents, children, grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins
quiz_questions.explanation: An extended family includes many relatives living nearby or together.

quiz_questions.question: What is a single-parent family?
quiz_questions.explanation: A single-parent family has one parent taking care of the children.

quiz_questions.question: How do families help each other?
options: By sharing meals and celebrating together
quiz_questions.correct_answer: By sharing meals and celebrating together
quiz_questions.explanation: Families show love by helping, sharing meals, and celebrating festivals together.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: Only nuclear families are real families.
quiz_questions.explanation: All types of families — nuclear, extended, single-parent — are real and special.

subject: Social & Citizenship Studies
content: Government is a group of people who make rules and decisions for the country. In Nigeria, we have three levels of government: federal (national), state, and local. The President is the leader of the federal government. Governors lead each state. Local government chairmen lead local areas. Government provides services like roads, schools, hospitals, and clean water. Government also makes laws to keep people safe. Voting is how citizens choose their leaders. When you grow up, you can vote too!
summary: Government makes rules and provides services. Nigeria has three levels: federal (President), state (Governor), local (Chairman). Citizens vote for leaders.
learning_objectives: Identify three levels of Nigerian government
nigerian_examples: The President lives and works in Abuja
Governors work in state capitals like Ikeja (Lagos) or Enugu
Local government chairmen help with local roads and markets

quiz_questions.question: What is government?
options: People who make rules and decisions for the country
quiz_questions.correct_answer: People who make rules and decisions for the country
quiz_questions.explanation: Government is the group of people who lead and make decisions for a country.

quiz_questions.question: How many levels of government does Nigeria have?
quiz_questions.explanation: Nigeria has federal, state, and local government levels.

quiz_questions.question: Who is the leader of the federal government?
quiz_questions.explanation: The President is the leader of Nigeria's federal government.

quiz_questions.question: What is one thing government provides?
quiz_questions.explanation: Government builds schools, hospitals, roads, and provides clean water.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: Children can vote in Nigerian elections.
quiz_questions.explanation: Only citizens who are 18 years or older can vote. Children will vote when they grow up.

subject: Social & Citizenship Studies
content: Transportation is how people and goods move from one place to another. In Nigeria, there are many types of transportation. On land, people use cars, buses, motorcycles (okadas), tricycles (keke napep), and trains. On water, people use boats and ferries on rivers and lagoons. In the air, airplanes fly between cities and countries. Transportation helps people go to school, work, market, and visit family. Different types of transportation are used for different distances and purposes. Always follow safety rules when using transportation.
summary: Transportation moves people and goods. Land: cars, buses, okadas, keke, trains. Water: boats, ferries. Air: airplanes. Different types for different needs.
nigerian_examples: Okadas and keke napep common in Lagos and other cities
Trains running between Abuja and Kaduna

quiz_questions.question: What is transportation?
options: How people and goods move from place to place
quiz_questions.correct_answer: How people and goods move from place to place
quiz_questions.explanation: Transportation includes all ways people and goods travel from one place to another.

quiz_questions.question: What is a common motorcycle taxi in Nigeria called?
quiz_questions.explanation: Okada is the common name for motorcycle taxis in Nigeria.

quiz_questions.question: What is a three-wheeled taxi called in Nigeria?
quiz_questions.explanation: Keke napep is a three-wheeled tricycle taxi common in Nigeria.

quiz_questions.question: Which transportation is used for traveling between cities far apart?
quiz_questions.explanation: Airplanes are used for long-distance travel between cities or countries.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: Water transportation is not used in Nigeria.
quiz_questions.explanation: Nigeria has rivers and lagoons where boats and ferries transport people and goods.

subject: Social & Citizenship Studies
content: Culture includes the food, language, music, dance, clothing, and traditions of a group of people. Nigeria has over 250 ethnic groups, each with its own culture. The three largest groups are Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa. Yoruba culture includes amala and ewedu soup, talking drums, and the Gelede festival. Igbo culture includes pounded yam and egusi soup, the omu (a symbol of authority), and the Mmanwu festival. Hausa culture includes tuwo shinkafa and miyan kuka, the durbar festival, and embroidered caps called hula. Nigerian culture is rich and beautiful!
summary: Culture includes food, language, music, dance, clothing. Nigeria has over 250 ethnic groups. Three largest: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa. Each has unique food, music, and festivals.
learning_objectives: Learn about Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa cultures
nigerian_examples: Yoruba talking drums used for communication
Hausa embroidered caps (hula) worn by men

quiz_questions.question: What does culture include?
options: Food, language, music, dance, clothing, and traditions
quiz_questions.correct_answer: Food, language, music, dance, clothing, and traditions
quiz_questions.explanation: Culture includes many things: food, language, music, dance, clothing, and traditions.

quiz_questions.question: How many ethnic groups does Nigeria have?
quiz_questions.explanation: Nigeria has over 250 different ethnic groups with unique cultures.

quiz_questions.question: Which food is associated with Yoruba culture?
quiz_questions.explanation: Amala and ewedu soup are traditional Yoruba foods.

quiz_questions.question: What is a talking drum?
options: A drum that cannot make sound
A Yoruba drum that can mimic speech tones
quiz_questions.correct_answer: A Yoruba drum that can mimic speech tones
quiz_questions.explanation: Talking drums in Yoruba culture can be played to mimic the tones of speech.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: All Nigerian ethnic groups have the same culture.
quiz_questions.explanation: Different ethnic groups have different foods, languages, music, and traditions.

subject: Social & Citizenship Studies
content: Festivals are special celebrations that happen every year. Nigeria has many festivals. Religious festivals include Christmas (Christian), Easter (Christian), Eid al-Fitr (Muslim), and Eid al-Adha (Muslim). Cultural festivals include the Eyo Festival in Lagos, Durbar in Kano, Calabar Carnival in Cross River, and New Yam Festival among the Igbo. During festivals, people wear special clothes, eat special foods, sing, dance, and spend time with family and friends. Festivals bring communities together and help preserve culture.
summary: Festivals are yearly celebrations. Religious: Christmas, Easter, Eid. Cultural: Eyo, Durbar, Calabar Carnival, New Yam Festival. Festivals bring people together.
learning_objectives: Distinguish between religious and cultural festivals
nigerian_examples: Eyo Festival with white-clad masquerades in Lagos
Calabar Carnival called 'Africa's Biggest Street Party'
Eid prayers at the Lagos Central Mosque

quiz_questions.question: Which festival is known as 'Africa's Biggest Street Party'?
quiz_questions.explanation: The Calabar Carnival in Cross River State is called 'Africa's Biggest Street Party'.

quiz_questions.question: Which festival features white-clad masquerades in Lagos?
quiz_questions.explanation: The Eyo Festival in Lagos features masquerades dressed in white.

quiz_questions.question: Which is a Muslim religious festival?
quiz_questions.explanation: Eid al-Fitr is a Muslim festival celebrating the end of Ramadan.

quiz_questions.question: Which festival involves horse riding and parades in northern Nigeria?
quiz_questions.explanation: Durbar is a colorful festival with horse riding, held in Kano and other northern cities.

quiz_questions.question: True or False: Festivals are only for eating food.
quiz_questions.explanation: Festivals include eating, but also music, dance, parades, prayers, and spending time with family.
